You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like March 2025, and the policy-rate and market figures support that.

- The fed funds rate is 4.33%, consistent with the 4.25–4.50% target range that held from December 2024 through August 2025.
- Unemployment is 4.2%, and the 3-month average payroll gain is 152k.
- US large-cap equity is down 7.6% over 3 months, with a drawdown of 9.3% from its 12-month high. That fits the early-2025 selloff, which was deepest in March and early April.
- The VIX is 24.17, up about 7.7 points over 3 months, which also fits March. The VIX was higher in April.
- Gold is up 19.5% over 3 months, consistent with the early-2025 rally.
- CPI is 2.41% year on year headline and 2.81% core, in line with the February 2025 readings (2.8% headline and 3.1% core). The core figure here looks a little low for that, so I considered April 2025 (core CPI 2.8%, headline 2.3%). But April's equity return was about -0.7% for the month and the 3-month return was around -4%, and May's VIX was lower. March fits better.
- The 10-year yield is 4.19%, in line with the end of March 2025 (about 4.23%).
- The 2-year yield is 3.65%, which is about right for end-March 2025 (3.89%) or April (3.60%). That makes it ambiguous.
- US large-cap equity is down 0.9% over 1 month, which fits March 2025 (S&P 500 about -5.6%) poorly. April 2025 was about -0.7%, which fits better. The 3-month return of -7.6% is also close to April's: Feb through April gave roughly -5% to -8%.
- The VIX at the end of April was about 24.7, which is close to the 24.17 shown. Developed ex-US equity is up 3.7% over 1 month, and the 3-month dollar change of -6.6% also fits April.

April 2025 therefore fits better than March.
